s: In the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, Chislev, after the people of Bethel sent Sharezer, Regem Melech and their men to ask the priests and prophets whether they should keep weeping in the fifth month as they had for years. The LORD of Armies answered through Zechariah, asking the people of the land and the priests whether their fasts of seventy years in the fifth and seventh months were truly for him, and noting that they ate and drank for themselves. He reminded them of the words of the former prophets, who had commanded true judgment, kindness, compassion, and no oppression of the widow, fatherless, foreigner, or poor. Their ancestors refused to listen, turned their backs, stopped their ears and hardened their hearts like flint, so great wrath came from the LORD. He declared that, as they would not listen when he called, he would not listen when they called, and he scattered them among the nations in a whirlwind, leaving the pleasant land desolate.

l: LORD of Armies, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 7
s: The LORD of Armies sends his word to Zechariah in response to the Bethel delegation, questioning whether the people's fasting was truly for him. He recalls his commands through the former prophets, and states that because they refused to listen he will not listen to them, and that he scattered them among the nations in a whirlwind.

l: Zechariah, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 7
s: Zechariah receives the LORD's word in the fourth year of King Darius, on the fourth day of Chislev. He relays the LORD's questions and rebuke to the people of the land and the priests, and the command to execute true judgment and show kindness.

l: people of Bethel, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 7
s: The people of Bethel send Sharezer, Regem Melech and their men to entreat the LORD's favor and ask the priests and prophets whether they should keep weeping in the fifth month as they have done for many years. Their question prompts the LORD's longer response about the purpose of fasting and obedience.

l: fast in the fifth month, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 7
s: The fast and mourning in the fifth month, along with the seventh, had been kept for seventy years. The LORD asks whether the people truly fasted to him, since they ate and drank only for themselves.

l: people of the land, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 7
s: The people of the land, together with the priests, are the ones Zechariah is told to address. They are questioned about whether their fasts of seventy years in the fifth and seventh months were really made to the LORD.

l: ancestors who refused to listen (they), The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 7
s: The ancestors refused to listen, turned their backs, stopped their ears and made their hearts as hard as flint, rejecting the law and the words sent by the LORD's Spirit through the former prophets. As a result great wrath came on them, the LORD would not listen when they called, and they were scattered by a whirlwind among nations they had not known.

l: commands of justice and kindness, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 7
s: The LORD of Armies commands people to execute true judgment, show kindness and compassion to one another, not oppress the widow, fatherless, foreigner or poor, and not devise evil against a brother in the heart. These are described as the words proclaimed by the former prophets when Jerusalem was inhabited and prosperous.

l: wrath of the LORD, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 7
s: Great wrath comes from the LORD of Armies because the people hardened their hearts and refused to hear the law and the words sent by his Spirit through the former prophets. It results in the LORD refusing to listen to their calls and scattering them among the nations.

l: pleasant land, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 7
s: The pleasant land is left desolate after the people are scattered, so that no one passes through or returns. The text says the people themselves made it desolate.

l: The Book of Zechariah, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 8
s: In Chapter 8, the LORD of Armies declares his jealous love for Zion and announces his return to dwell in Jerusalem, which will be called the City of Truth. He promises a restored city with old people and playing children, the gathering of his people from east and west, and an end to the poverty and insecurity of former days for the remnant. He turns the house of Judah and house of Israel from a curse into a blessing, commands them to speak truth, judge with truth and peace, and avoid evil plots and false oaths. The fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months will become joyful feasts. Many peoples and strong nations will come to Jerusalem to seek the LORD, and ten men from every language will grasp the skirt of a Jew because God is with them.

l: LORD of Armies, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 8
s: The LORD of Armies declares that he is jealous for Zion with great wrath, has returned to dwell in Jerusalem, and will save his people from east and west to be their God in truth and righteousness. He explains that as he once planned evil against the fathers' generation and did not relent, he now plans good for Jerusalem and Judah, and he commands truthfulness while hating evil plots and false oaths.

l: Zion, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 8
s: Zion is the object of the LORD of Armies' great jealousy and great wrath. He states that he has returned to Zion.

l: Jerusalem, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 8
s: Jerusalem is where the LORD will dwell, and it will be called The City of Truth, with the mountain of the LORD called The Holy Mountain. Its streets will hold old men and women with staffs and be full of playing boys and girls, its people gathered from east and west will dwell within it, and many peoples will come there to seek the LORD.

l: remnant of this people, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 8
s: The remnant is told that its present marvel is not too marvelous for the LORD, and that he will no longer treat it as in the former days of no wages, no peace, and strife with neighbors. It will inherit peaceful seed, fruitful vine, productive ground, and dew from heaven.

l: Judah, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 8
s: The house of Judah, together with the house of Israel, was a curse among the nations but is promised salvation and a role as a blessing, with the command not to be afraid and to let their hands be strong. The LORD plans good for Judah, and its fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months will become joy, gladness, and cheerful feasts. A Jew is also the one whose skirt ten men from the nations will take hold of.

l: many peoples and strong nations, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 8
s: Many peoples, inhabitants of many cities, and strong nations are foretold to come to Jerusalem to entreat the favor of the LORD and seek the LORD of Armies, urging one another to go speedily. Ten men from all the languages of the nations will take hold of a Jew's skirt, saying they will go with him because they have heard God is with them.

l: truth and peace, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 8
s: Truth and peace are what the people are commanded to practice: speaking truth to neighbors and executing the judgment of truth and peace in the gates. The people are told to love truth and peace, in connection with the fasts becoming joyful feasts.

l: The Book of Zechariah, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 9
s: Chapter 9 opens with the LORD's word against Hadrach, Damascus, Hamath, Tyre and Sidon, announcing that Tyre's wealth and stronghold will not save her from being struck and burned. The Philistine cities Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and Ashdod will fear and lose their king and pride, though a remnant will belong to God. The LORD promises to encamp around his house, and the daughter of Zion is told to rejoice because her righteous, lowly King comes riding a donkey, cutting off chariot, horse and bow and speaking peace to the nations. The LORD frees the prisoners of hope, promises them double restoration, and arms Judah and Ephraim like a bow and sword against Greece. He appears with lightning and the trumpet, defends and saves his people like a flock, and the chapter ends with praise of his goodness and the flourishing of young men and virgins.

l: LORD of Armies, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 9
s: The LORD speaks against Hadrach, Damascus, Hamath, Tyre, Sidon and the Philistine cities, dispossessing Tyre and cutting off the pride of the Philistines. He encamps around his house, frees prisoners, promises double restoration, bends Judah as a bow, appears with lightning and the trumpet, and saves his people as a flock. His goodness and beauty are praised as great.

l: Tyre, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 9
s: Tyre is condemned as very wise; she built a stronghold and heaped up silver like dust and gold like mire. The Lord will dispossess her, strike her power in the sea, and she will be devoured with fire.

l: Philistines, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 9
s: The Philistine cities Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and Ashdod will see Tyre's fate and fear, with Gaza writhing and losing its king and Ashkelon left uninhabited. Foreigners will dwell in Ashdod, and the LORD will cut off Philistine pride, take blood and abominations from their mouths, and leave a remnant for God, like a chieftain in Judah, with Ekron as a Jebusite.

l: Judah, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 9
s: Judah is described as a chieftain-like place for the Philistine remnant and as a bow the LORD bends for himself, loaded with Ephraim. Its sons are to be stirred up against the sons of Greece.

l: Zion, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 9
s: The daughter of Zion is told to rejoice greatly because her King comes to her. Her sons will be stirred up against Greece, and she will be made like the sword of a mighty man.

l: Jerusalem, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 9
s: The daughter of Jerusalem is told to shout because her King comes. The LORD will cut off the horse from Jerusalem.

l: king (the coming King of Zion), The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 9
s: The King comes to Zion righteous, having salvation, lowly and riding on a donkey, a colt, the foal of a donkey. He will speak peace to the nations, and his dominion will stretch from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth.

l: prisoners of hope, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 9
s: Because of the blood of the covenant, the LORD has set the prisoners free from the waterless pit. They are told to turn to the stronghold and are promised that he will restore double to them.

l: Judah's people (the LORD's people), The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 9
s: The LORD's people are defended by the LORD of Armies, overcome with sling stones, and drink and roar as with wine, filled like bowls and like the corners of the altar. He saves them as a flock, and they are like jewels of a crown lifted over his land, with grain and new wine making the young men and virgins flourish.

l: The Book of Zechariah, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 10
s: Chapter 10 urges the people to ask the LORD for spring rain, contrasting him with the teraphim and diviners who speak vanity and false dreams, leaving the people like sheep with no shepherd. The LORD's anger is kindled against the shepherds and male goats, and he visits his flock, the house of Judah, making them like a majestic war horse. From Judah will come the cornerstone, tent peg, battle bow and every ruler, and they will fight and confound the horse riders because the LORD is with them. The LORD promises to strengthen Judah and save the house of Joseph, bringing them back with mercy, so that Ephraim rejoices like a mighty man. He will signal, gather, redeem and sow them among the peoples, then return them from Egypt and Assyria to Gilead and Lebanon, while Assyria's pride is brought down and Egypt's scepter departs.

l: LORD of Armies, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 10
s: The LORD is the one to ask for rain, making storm clouds and giving showers to everyone. He is angry at the shepherds, visits his flock, and promises to strengthen, save, redeem, gather and return his people, hearing them and having mercy on them. He will bring down Assyria's pride and Egypt's scepter, and the people will walk in his name.

l: Judah, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 10
s: The house of Judah is the LORD's flock, which he has visited and will make like his majestic horse in battle. The LORD says he will strengthen it, and from it will come the cornerstone, tent peg, battle bow and every ruler.

l: house of Joseph, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 10
s: The LORD says he will save the house of Joseph and bring them back out of mercy. They will be as though he had not cast them off.

l: Ephraim, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 10
s: Ephraim will be like a mighty man, and their heart will rejoice as with wine. Their children will see it and rejoice, being glad in the LORD.

l: Assyria, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 10
s: Assyria is a land from which the LORD will gather his people. Its pride will be brought down.

l: Egypt, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 10
s: Egypt is a land from which the LORD will bring his people again. Its scepter will depart, and the depths of the Nile will dry up.

l: shepherds, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 10
s: The shepherds draw the LORD's kindled anger, and he says he will punish the male goats. The people go like oppressed sheep because there is no shepherd.

l: people of Israel (returning exiles), The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 10
s: The people are promised that the LORD will signal, gather and redeem them, and that they will increase as before. Sown among the peoples, they will remember him in far countries, then return with their children to Gilead and Lebanon, where there won't be room enough for them. They will walk up and down in his name.

l: The Book of Zechariah, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 11
s: Chapter 11 opens with a lament over the ruin of Lebanon's cedars, the oaks of Bashan, and the shepherds' glory. The LORD tells the narrator to feed the flock of slaughter, whose buyers and sellers exploit them and whose own shepherds show no pity, and declares He will no longer pity the inhabitants of the land. The narrator takes two staffs, Favor and Union, cuts off three shepherds in one month, and then cuts Favor apart to break the covenant with all the peoples. He is paid thirty pieces of silver as wages, which the LORD tells him to throw to the potter in the LORD's house, and he then cuts Union apart to break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel. The LORD commands him to take the equipment of a foolish shepherd, announces a worthless shepherd who will abandon the flock, and pronounces that the sword will wither his arm and blind his right eye.

l: LORD of Armies, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 11
s: The LORD commands the narrator to feed the flock of slaughter and declares He will no longer pity the inhabitants of the land, delivering them into the hands of neighbors and kings. He tells the narrator to throw the handsome price to the potter, orders him to take the equipment of a foolish shepherd, and announces a worthless shepherd whose arm and right eye will be struck by the sword.

l: narrator (the shepherd speaking), The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 11
s: The narrator feeds the flock to be slaughtered, takes two staffs called Favor and Union, and cuts off three shepherds in one month. He refuses to keep feeding the flock, breaks both staffs, is paid thirty pieces of silver, and throws them to the potter in the LORD's house at the LORD's command. He is then told to take the equipment of a foolish shepherd.

l: shepherds (of the flock), The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 11
s: The shepherds wail because their glory is destroyed, and they show no pity to the flock. The narrator cuts off three shepherds in one month because his soul was weary of them and their soul loathed him.

l: flock of slaughter, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 11
s: The flock is slaughtered by buyers who go unpunished and sold by sellers who thank the LORD for their riches, while its own shepherds don't pity it. The narrator feeds it, especially the oppressed, then declines to feed it further and lets the dying die and the survivors eat each other's flesh. The poor of the flock who listened to him recognize the broken staff as the LORD's word.

l: inhabitants of the land, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 11
s: The LORD says He will no longer pity the inhabitants of the land. He will deliver each man into the hand of his neighbor and of his king, and they will strike the land without deliverance from Him.

l: Favor, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 11
s: Favor is one of two staffs the narrator takes for himself. He cuts it apart to break the covenant he had made with all the peoples, and its breaking shows the poor of the flock that it was the LORD's word.

l: Union, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 11
s: Union is the second staff the narrator takes. He cuts it apart to break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.

l: thirty pieces of silver, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 11
s: The thirty pieces of silver are weighed out as the narrator's wages, a handsome price at which he was valued. At the LORD's command he throws them to the potter in the LORD's house.

l: foolish shepherd, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 11
s: The narrator is told to take the equipment of a foolish shepherd. The LORD says He will raise up such a shepherd, who will neither visit the cut off, seek the scattered, heal the broken, nor feed the sound, but will eat the fat sheep and tear their hoofs. Woe is pronounced on him as a worthless shepherd who leaves the flock, with his arm to wither and his right eye to be blinded.

l: The Book of Zechariah, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 12
s: Chapter 12 is a revelation from the LORD, who stretches out the heavens, lays the earth's foundation, and forms the human spirit, concerning Israel. He declares that Jerusalem will become a cup of reeling and a burdensome stone to the surrounding peoples, who will gather against it and be wounded, while he strikes their horses and riders with terror, madness, and blindness. The chieftains of Judah will become like a pan of fire and a flaming torch that devour the surrounding peoples, and the LORD will save Judah's tents first and defend Jerusalem's inhabitants, making even the feeble like David. He will seek to destroy all nations that come against Jerusalem and will pour out a spirit of grace and supplication on David's house and Jerusalem's inhabitants. They will look to the one they pierced and mourn for him as for an only son, in a great mourning with each family and their wives apart.

l: LORD of Armies, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 12
s: The LORD, described as the one who stretches out the heavens, lays the earth's foundation, and forms the spirit of man, announces that he will make Jerusalem a cup of reeling and a burdensome stone, strike the enemy horses and riders, and seek to destroy all nations that come against Jerusalem. He will save Judah's tents first, defend Jerusalem's inhabitants, and pour out a spirit of grace and supplication on David's house and Jerusalem's inhabitants. He speaks of himself as the one whom they have pierced.

l: Jerusalem, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 12
s: Jerusalem is made a cup of reeling and a burdensome stone for the surrounding peoples, and all the nations of the earth will gather against it. The LORD will defend its inhabitants, the feeble among them will be like David, and it will dwell again in its own place. A great mourning will take place there, like the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddo.

l: Judah, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 12
s: Judah is affected by the siege against Jerusalem, but the LORD will open his eyes on the house of Judah and save the tents of Judah first, so that the glory of David's house and of Jerusalem's inhabitants is not magnified above Judah.

l: chieftains of Judah, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 12
s: The chieftains of Judah say in their heart that the inhabitants of Jerusalem are their strength in the LORD of Armies their God. The LORD will make them like a pan of fire among wood and a flaming torch among sheaves, devouring the surrounding peoples on the right hand and on the left.

l: nations (the peoples surrounding Jerusalem), The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 12
s: The surrounding peoples will drink from the cup of reeling that Jerusalem becomes, and all the nations of the earth will be gathered against it. Those who burden themselves with the stone will be severely wounded, their horses will be struck with blindness, and the LORD will seek to destroy them. The chieftains of Judah will devour the surrounding peoples.

l: house of David, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 12
s: The house of David will be like God, like the LORD's angel before them, and the LORD will pour on it the spirit of grace and of supplication. Its glory is not to be magnified above Judah, and its family mourns apart, with their wives apart, along with the family of the house of Nathan.

l: the pierced one, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 12
s: The pierced one is the one to whom the people will look, the LORD speaking of him as the one they have pierced. They will mourn for him as one mourns for an only son and grieve bitterly as for a firstborn.

l: mourning in Jerusalem, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 12
s: A great mourning will occur in that day, compared to the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddo. The whole land mourns with every family apart and their wives apart, including the families of the house of David, the house of Nathan, the house of Levi, the Shimeites, and all remaining families.

l: The Book of Zechariah, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 13
s: Chapter 13 describes a coming day when the LORD of Armies opens a fountain to David's house and the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and uncleanness. He will cut off the names of idols and remove the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land. Anyone who still prophesies will be killed by his own parents for speaking lies in the LORD's name, and prophets will be ashamed and deny their calling. The LORD then calls the sword against his shepherd, whose being struck scatters the sheep and turns his hand against the little ones. Two parts of the land will be cut off and die, while the remaining third will be put through fire and refined like silver and gold, call on the LORD's name, and be acknowledged as his people.

l: LORD of Armies, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 13
s: The LORD of Armies promises that in that day he will open a fountain for sin and uncleanness, cut off the names of idols, and remove the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land. He summons the sword against his shepherd and strikes him, scattering the sheep and turning his hand against the little ones. He causes two parts of the land to be cut off, refines the remaining third, hears them when they call on his name, and declares them his people.

l: fountain (opened to David's house), The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 13
s: A fountain will be opened in that day to David's house and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. Its purpose is stated as being for sin and for uncleanness.

l: prophets, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 13
s: The prophets, along with the spirit of impurity, will be caused to pass out of the land. Anyone who still prophesies will be told by his father and mother that he must die for speaking lies in the LORD's name, and they will stab him. The prophets will be ashamed of their visions, will not wear a hairy mantle to deceive, and will deny being prophets, claiming instead to be tillers of the ground and bondservants since youth. When asked about wounds between his arms, one says he was wounded in the house of his friends.

l: shepherd (the LORD's shepherd), The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 13
s: The LORD calls the sword to awake against his shepherd, described as the man close to him. He commands that the shepherd be struck, and the result is that the sheep will be scattered.

l: land, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 13
s: The land will be purged of the names of idols, which will be remembered no more, and of the prophets and the spirit of impurity. Two parts of it will be cut off and die, while the third part will be left in it.

l: people of the land (the refined third), The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 13
s: The third part left in the land will be brought into the fire. They will call on the LORD's name and he will hear them. The LORD will say, 'It is my people,' and they will answer, 'The LORD is my God.'

l: refining by fire, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 13
s: The LORD will bring the surviving third into the fire, refining them as silver is refined and testing them as gold is tested. The outcome is that they call on his name, he hears them, and they are affirmed as his people.

l: The Book of Zechariah, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 14
s: Chapter 14 describes a coming day of the LORD in which all nations are gathered against Jerusalem, which is taken and half its people exiled. The LORD then goes out to fight, stands on the Mount of Olives and splits it, creating a valley of escape. A plague strikes the attacking peoples, and Judah fights at Jerusalem and gathers great wealth. The LORD becomes King over all the earth, living waters flow from Jerusalem, and the land is made like the Arabah while Jerusalem dwells safely. Surviving nations must go up yearly to keep the feast of booths or receive no rain, as Egypt is warned, and everything in Jerusalem and Judah becomes holy to the LORD.

l: LORD of Armies, The Book of Zechariah, Chapter 14
s: The LORD gathers the nations against Jerusalem, then goes out to fight them and stands on the Mount of Olives. He strikes the peoples with a plague and a great panic, and becomes King over all the earth, one with one name. He is worshiped as the LORD of Armies, and he withholds rain from nations that do not come to keep the feast of booths.
